questions.question: From a point P on a level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30°. If the tower is 110sqrt 3 m high, what is the distance (in m) of point P from the foot of the tower?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The angle of elevation of the top of a tower = 30°

The height of the tower = 110√3 m

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c977df5e511ac02a2743ce832be3ac9ca12693d9dddf876bb7e08a0d885675c.png] **

AB = 110√3 m

tan 30° = AB/PB

⇒ 1/√3 = 110√3/PB

⇒ PB = 110√3 × √3

⇒ PB = 110 × 3 = 330 m

**∴ The distance (in m) of point P from the foot of the tower is 330 m**

questions.question: As observed from the top of a lighthouse, 42 m high above sea-level, the angle of depression of a ship sailing directly towards it changes from 30° to 45°. The distance travelled by the ship during the period of observation is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the angle of elevation (or depression) of a tower of height h changes from θ₁ to θ₂ as an object moves directly towards it, the distance travelled is:

Distance = h × (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)

Here, h = 42 m, θ₁ = 30°, θ₂ = 45°

Distance = 42 × (cot 30° − cot 45°)

Distance = 42 × (√3 − 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 − 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e7eb57492f4e8ed7e1520931e65b2310f3a7ad59fb5b406a3d3d4ea60fbae88.png] 

**Given:**

Height of the lighthouse (AB) = 42 m

Angle of depression at initial position C = 30° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ACB = 30°

Angle of depression at final position D = 45° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ADB = 45°

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

In right-angled triangle ΔABD,

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1 = 42 ÷ BD

⇒ BD = 42 m

In right-angled triangle ΔABC,

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = 42 ÷ BC

⇒ BC = 42√3 m

The distance travelled by the ship is CD, which is the difference between BC and BD.

⇒ Distance CD = BC − BD

⇒ Distance CD = 42√3 − 42

⇒ Distance CD = 42(√3 − 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 − 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heights and Distances (Trigonometry)

The angle of elevation is the angle formed between the horizontal reference line and the line of sight when looking up at an object. The angle of depression is the angle formed when looking down from a height.

Two Objects on the Same Side

If two objects are observed on the ground from a tower of height h at angles θ₁ and θ₂, the distance separating them is easily calculated as h(cot θ₁ − cot θ₂).

Two Objects on Opposite Sides

When two objects are situated on opposite sides of a central tower of height h, having respective angles of elevation θ₁ and θ₂, the total distance between them is h(cot θ₁ + cot θ₂).

questions.question: The length of the shadow on the ground of a tall tree of height 45 m is 15sqrt{3} m. What is the angle (in degrees) of elevation of the sun?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The height of the tree = 45 m

The length of the shadow of the tree = 15√3 m

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92dedf62174efeddf656abf670ecdb664ee626d074477d1f80085da24720daf2.png] 

The height of the tree (BC) = 45 m

The length of the shadow of the tree (AB) = 15√3 m

The angle of elevation = ∠CAB

tan ∠CAB = BC/AB

⇒ tan ∠CAB = 45/15√3

⇒ tan ∠CAB = √3 = tan 60°

⇒ ∠CAB = 60°

**∴ The angle (in degrees) of elevation of the sun is 60°**

questions.question: A kite flying at a height of 120 m is attached to a string which makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal. What is the length (in m) of the string?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The height where the kite is flying = 120 m

The angle is made by the string = 60°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7940532fedf1c7d758730e162a18b32968c534115d5edc33f65cc5507d430bb8.png] 

The distance of kite from the ground (AB) = 120 m and ∠ACB = 60°

The length of the string = AC

So, sin 60° = AB/AC

⇒ √3/2 = 120/AC [∵ sin 60° = 3/2]

⇒ AC = (120 × 2)/√3 = 80√3 m

**∴ The length (in m) of the string is 80√3 m**

questions.question: The length of the shadow of a vertical tower on level ground increases by 10 m when the altitude of the sun changes from 45° to 30°. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for height (h) when shadow increases by distance (d) as angle changes from θ₁ to θ₂:

h = d ÷ (cot θ₂ − cot θ₁)

Here, d = 10 m, θ₂ = 30°, and θ₁ = 45°

h = 10 ÷ (cot 30° − cot 45°) = 10 ÷ (√3 − 1)

By rationalizing: h = [10 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)] = 10(√3 + 1) ÷ 2 = 5(√3 + 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 5(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in shadow length (CD) = 10 m

Angle of elevation at initial position (C) = 45°

Angle of elevation at final position (D) = 30°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/590b05f974baeb16c07ef7da327a1c5054d48442e9d8b3a3c86b884edea94ce7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the height of the tower AB be h.

⇒ In right-angled ▵ABC, tan 45° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 = h ÷ BC → BC = h

⇒ In right-angled ▵ABD, tan 30° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = h ÷ BD → BD = h√3

⇒ Given CD = BD − BC = 10 m

⇒ h√3 − h = 10

⇒ h(√3 − 1) = 10

⇒ h = 10 ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ h = [10 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = 10(√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 10(√3 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ h = 5(√3 + 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 5(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. Cot is the reciprocal: cot 30° = √3, cot 45° = 1, cot 60° = 1/√3.

Shadow and Angle Relation

As the altitude of the sun decreases, the length of the shadow of a vertical object increases.

Rationalization Rule

To rationalize a denominator of the form (a − √b), multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate (a + √b).</p
